body.x: ARK Inc. (CEO Hyung Hoi Kim) participated in the Global Media Meetup on September 1, an event introducing Korean startups’ products and technologies to global markets. The meetup was co-hosted by AVING News and U.S.-based tech media outlet Ubergizmo, with a focus on CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and CES participants.

Founded in 2018 by Hyung Hoi Kim, head of the Biomedical Research Institute at Pusan National University Hospital, and a team of ophthalmologists, ARK developed ‘OREUM,’ an integrated solution platform that broadly addresses chronic diseases. The platform combines ARK’s proprietary AI-based solutions with third-party medical AI tools to enable early diagnosis of retinal, cardiovascular, and chronic kidney diseases. Commercialization began in September.

According to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency’s 2023 report on chronic diseases, 276,930 people died from chronic diseases in 2022, accounting for 74.3% of total deaths. The numbers—244,729 in 2020 and 252,993 in 2021—show a steady increase each year.

body.cap: Flow chart of ARK’s chronic disease integrated diagnostic platform OREUM | Image by ARK

body.x: While the number of chronic disease patients is rising, there is a shortage of specialized medical professionals worldwide. Patients often waste time and money visiting multiple hospitals. ARK’s OREUM offers a solution to reduce social costs and improve convenience for both patients and doctors.

OREUM, ARK’s flagship solution for CES 2026, provides integrated early diagnosis and management for six chronic conditions: diabetes, retinal disease, cardiovascular disease, autonomic nervous system disease, chronic kidney disease, and hypertension. It simplifies diagnostic processes by identifying cardiovascular and kidney diseases through retinal images alone.

To achieve this, ARK trained its deep learning model using data from patients who underwent simultaneous retinal imaging, vascular CT scans, and eGFR tests, thereby capturing correlations between the datasets. The model converts retinal fundus images into byte arrays for computer processing and categorizes them as normal or abnormal.

ARK improved reliability through iterative learning. The AI model’s outputs were compared with physicians’ diagnoses, and differences were converted into loss values for optimization using stochastic gradient descent. This approach, the company said, enhanced accuracy to match professional diagnoses closely.

body.cap: Kyle In Yong Lee presents at the Global Media Meetup with Ubergizmo at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: OREUM also integrates with PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System), used by Korean hospitals for standardized imaging. ARK’s gateway program “ARK-Bridge” automatically converts diverse file formats (JPG, PNG, PDF) into DICOM, the sole file type recognized by PACS.

“OREUM integrates diverse medical imaging data into a single DICOM file and connects seamlessly with PACS,” said Kyle In Yong Lee. “This allows us to provide patients with personalized, visual health reports that summarize their conditions clearly.”
He added, “OREUM uses APIs to transmit patient information in de-identified form, enabling broad compatibility with other AI solutions and ensuring high utility across diverse medical environments.”

ARK has already distributed its retinal disease diagnostic software to over 1,000 institutions and signed an exclusive domestic distribution contract with a major pharmaceutical company for OREUM. The company’s accumulated revenue has surpassed 5 billion KRW, and it expects rapid growth. Beginning with nationwide distribution in Korea, ARK plans to establish itself in the domestic AI medical software market while building networks in key export destinations. CES 2026 in Las Vegas will serve as the launchpad for global expansion.

body.cap: ARK staff and Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen (center) pose for a photo at the Global Media Meetup at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: “The core value of OREUM lies in expanding the medical capabilities of general and small hospitals,” Lee said. “This could significantly improve access to specialized medical services in underdeveloped or emerging markets.”

He added, “We set priority export markets as Vietnam, Thailand, and Taiwan. With CE and ISO certifications already in place, we can streamline our market entry. CES is the ideal place to meet decision-makers and experts from North America, Europe, and around the world, making it the perfect opportunity to secure networks for our goals.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
